subject: general
question: When did Mahatma Gandhi return to India from South Africa?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Fri Jan 01 1915 00:00:00 GMT+0530 (India Standard Time)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mahatma Gandhi returned to India from South Africa on **9th January 1915**, which is commemorated as **Pravasi Bharatiya Divas** (Non-Resident Indian Day).
 
• Gandhi's return marked the beginning of a significant chapter in India's struggle for independence, as he became a prominent leader in the Indian National Movement.
 
• He spent 21 years in South Africa, where he developed his political views, ethics, and leadership skills, particularly his advocacy for nonviolent protest (Satyagraha).
 
• Upon his return, Gandhi traveled extensively across India to understand the plight of the common people and gradually became involved in various movements against British colonial rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gandhi's Early Life and Education**

 
 
• Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi, later known as Mahatma Gandhi, was born on 2nd October 1869 in Porbandar, Gujarat.
 
• He studied law at the Inner Temple in London and became a barrister in 1891.
 
 
 
• **Gandhi in South Africa**
 
 
• Gandhi moved to South Africa in 1893 to practice law and stayed there for 21 years.
 
• He faced racial discrimination and injustices, which inspired him to fight for civil rights and justice.
 
• Gandhi pioneered the concept of Satyagraha (truth and nonviolent resistance) during his time in South Africa.
 
 
 
• **Gandhi's Role in Indian Independence Movement**
 
 
• After returning to India in 1915, Gandhi joined the Indian National Congress and became a leader in the Indian independence movement.
 
• He led several nationwide campaigns for various social causes and for Swaraj (self-rule), including the Non-Cooperation Movement, Civil Disobedience Movement, and Quit India Movement.
 
• Gandhi's philosophy of nonviolence and peaceful protests influenced many leaders and movements worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Legacy**
 
 
• Mahatma Gandhi is remembered as the Father of the Nation in India.
 
• His birthday, 2nd October, is celebrated as Gandhi Jayanti and is also observed as the International Day of Non-Violence.
 
• Gandhi's teachings continue to inspire movements for civil rights and social justice globally.
